own_solution.law: Snell's law gives theta_t = asin(sin(75 degrees)/1.5). The p-polarised power reflectance is R = [(1.5 cos(75 degrees) - cos(theta_t))/(1.5 cos(75 degrees) + cos(theta_t))]^2 = 0.106765. Energy conservation gives Pt = Pin(1-R). Without amplification Pin = 5 mW; with an amplifier adding q to the current beam, Pin = 5 mW + q.
assumptions: The glass is an ordinary homogeneous, isotropic, nonmagnetic optical medium.
Propagation to the interface has negligible loss.
The entire incident beam strikes the glass surface.

All disconnected and cancelling variants retain 4.46617 mW at every listed value. The area cancels when irradiance is integrated over the corresponding beam area; interpreting 'covers an area' as a surface footprint also leaves total transmitted power unchanged.
